title: AssuranceCandidate — the pre-decision binding (root) + AssuranceSummary ($defs/assuranceSummary)
description: Both documents are controller-generated bindings, and the line between them is temporal: the AssuranceCandidate exists BEFORE the user's FINAL decision and therefore cannot reference it, while exactly one AssuranceSummary is generated AFTER it (invariant 12, N2-A7). That is why the candidate below has no field for a decision, a summary or an outcome — not by convention but by additionalProperties:false, so a self-binding candidate is unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. The controller binds refs and may never restate evidence with stronger epistemic meaning (V3-D5, N2-A9): every disclosure it carries must name the document it came from, so the controller cannot author a claim of its own.

candidate_ref.description: The exact payload the user is being asked to decide about.

bound_by.description: The controller that assembled this binding. Assembling is not judging.

check_result_refs.description: Absent when the run produced none — every obligation may be review_only. Absence is never an empty placeholder.

review_refs.description: The FULL, plus the targeted VERIFY when a repair happened. Capped at two because no third review round exists (V3-D6, N2-A11) — a cap the schema can hold and therefore should.

unresolved_finding_ids.description: Blocking findings still open at the moment of binding, by ID only. Copying an identity is a binding; copying the finding's text would be the controller restating a reviewer's claim (N2-A9).

disclosures.description: What the user should know before deciding. Present only when there is something to disclose.

included.description: Whether the governance-frontmatter scan actually ran in this run.

result_ref.description: The CheckResult of the command_exit request that ran it. Required when included, so 'we ran it' is a reference to evidence rather than an assertion.

skip_reason.description: Why it did not run. Required when it did not.

governanceScanState.description: Discharges N1-R2. The R4 governance scan was mechanical and reachable after N1, but nothing obliged a run to invoke it, so an operator who never called it got no signal at all. This field makes the state REPORTED either way: the run cannot reach a FINAL decision without saying whether the scan ran, and a skip is a visible, reasoned skip rather than silence. It deliberately does not force the scan to run — forcing verification is the wrong endpoint; making the unverified visible is the reachable one.

source_ref.description: The owner-authored document this disclosure came from. Required, which is what stops the controller from inventing one: a disclosure with no source would be the controller speaking in its own voice about evidence it does not own (V3-D5).

promoted_to.description: Where the accepted payload was promoted to. Explicit and recorded, never implied by acceptance (invariant 13).

then.description: A promotion that does not say where it went and why is not a recorded promotion.

assurance_candidate_ref.description: The exact pre-decision binding this terminates. Bound by digest so the summary cannot be re-pointed at a different candidate after the fact.

final_decision_ref.description: The exact user FINAL decision. Required: a summary generated without one would be the controller closing a run the user never closed.

outcome.description: A copy of the user's own decision, which the user owns — the controller binds it, it does not judge it. This is the one restatement that is not a strengthening (V3-D4, N2-A9).

limitations.description: The limitations the user acknowledged. Required for ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATIONS — an acceptance 'with limitations' that lists none is an unqualified acceptance wearing a qualifier.

then.description: REJECT and REPLAN never promote payload (invariant 13, N2-A8). Held at the schema layer as well as in the flow, because this is the one place where a wrong value silently ships bytes the user declined.

assuranceSummary.description: The single terminal binding, generated only after FINAL (sole owner: controller).
